'''Sanchez:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} | title = [[List of governors of New Mexico|Governor]] | before_election = [[Gary Johnson]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bill Richardson]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNM}} The '''2002 New Mexico gubernatorial election''' was a race for the [[Governor of New Mexico]]. The winner of the election held on November 5, 2002, served from January 1, 2003, until January 1, 2007. Incumbent Republican [[Gary Johnson]] was [[Term limits in the United States|term limited]]. Former U.S. Congressman [[Bill Richardson]] won the election. Green Party nominee David Bacon received over 5% of the total vote, including over 11% in [[Santa Fe County, New Mexico|Santa Fe County]], which was his best showing. ==Primary election== ===Democratic party=== ====Candidates==== *[[Bill Richardson (politician)|Bill Richardson]], former [[United States Secretary of Energy]], former [[United States Ambassador to the United Nations]] and former [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] *Mike Nalley (write-in) ====Results==== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results{{Cite web|title=Election Results 2002 |url=https://www.sos.nm.gov/voting-and-elections/election-results/past-election-results-2002/ |publisher=New Mexico Secretary of State|access-date=July 29, 2024}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Bill Richardson]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 147,524 | percentage = 99.80% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Mike Nalley (write-in) | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 294 | percentage = 0.20% }} {{Election box total no change | votes =147,818 | percentage =100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ===Republican party=== ====Candidates==== *Gilbert S.
